name: Union of Soviet Socialist Republics

areaKm2.note: world_1938 USSR polygon = ~21.13M km2 computed on the sphere (low); plus the 1939-40 annexations (eastern Poland, Baltic states, Bessarabia, Karelian Isthmus, ~0.7M km2) and Tuva (Oct 1944) = ~22.1-22.4M km2 (mid/high). In June 1944 Belorussia, the Baltic and part of Ukraine were still German-occupied.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1944 = 182,500k (high); 194M in June 1941 less ~27M war dead and losses by the end of the war; ~170-175M in mid-1944 within the 1941 borders (mid, reconstruction).

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) urban share Russia 1940 = 35.3% (present-day Russia, high); 1939 Soviet census 32.9% (mid). Low = COW upop/tpop 1944 = 29,862/182,500 = 0.16 (cities over 100,000).

activePersonnel.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-5: Soviet armed forces 11,858,000 in 1943 (low) and 12,225,000 in 1944 (mid, high), incl. hospitals, PVO, navy and NKVD troops. Snapshot: June 1944. Check: COW NMC v7 milper 1944 = 6,100k (annual averages, not the snapshot-date strength).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Recovering wounded, men in liberated territories being re-conscripted (1944 call-ups in Ukraine and Belorussia).

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Glantz and House, When Titans Clashed (isbn:0-7006-0717-X), not read from a fetched source. Artillery, tank, engineer, signal and rear-service troops, PVO, VVS (~1M), navy (~0.5M), hospitals (~1M), reserve units (Glantz and House, appendix tables). Derived as active minus infantry and cavalry.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Glantz and House, When Titans Clashed (isbn:0-7006-0717-X), not read from a fetched source. ~500 rifle divisions at 5,000-7,000 men, ~40-45% riflemen, plus rifle brigades and fortified regions.

count.note: Educated guess. 1941 totals read from the Soviet Navy page; 1944 losses and additions recalled, not read from a fetched source. Battleships, cruisers and destroyers. Cited page: 3 battleships and 7 cruisers in 1941; by June 1944 2 Gangut-class battleships (Marat a floating battery), ~9 cruisers incl. 2 new in the Pacific; Royal Sovereign and USS Milwaukee transferred in spring 1944 (high) (Conway's 1922-1946) = 11/13/15. Destroyers: 59 in 1941 (cited page); ~34 lost, ~10 added by 1944 (Conway's 1922-1946) = 38/45/55. Role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: destroyers moved from ships_minor, which is now omitted.

quality.note: Count-weighted mean (mid counts) of battleships/cruisers 0.5/0.55/0.6 (13) and destroyers 0.6/0.65/0.7 (45), role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries. Rubric rows: quality 0.5 and 0.5-0.75. Evidence: old battleships, modern Kirov-class cruisers, Gnevny and Soobrazitelny destroyers

training.note: Count-weighted mean (mid counts) of battleships/cruisers 0.45/0.5/0.55 (13) and destroyers 0.5/0.55/0.6 (45), role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries. Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: little open-sea action

count.note: Educated guess. 1941 total read from the Soviet Navy page; 1944 losses and additions recalled, not read from a fetched source. Cited page: 218 submarines in 1941; ~100 lost by 1944, new construction mostly in the Pacific (Conway's 1922-1946).

communications.note: Anchor: between 7 and 8. Evidence: Lend-Lease radios and telephone wire; front-level radio nets

air.note: Anchor: 8 (1943). Evidence: Yak-3, La-7, Il-2, Tu-2; no jets

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv): USSR 1940 = 3,417 (high); the 'Russia' series 1944 = 2,392 (low). Harrison 1998 (https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/soc/economics/staff/mharrison/public/ww2overview1998.pdf) Soviet GDP 1944 = 362 vs 417 (bn 1990 int$) in 1940, with ~10% fewer people: 3,417 x 0.87 / 0.9 = ~3,300; mid 3,100.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-8: Soviet military burden 53% in 1944 (61% in 1942-43, high).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Industry incl. war production ~40% of output after evacuation to the Urals.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of employment. Cited page: 1939 census population 170.5M of which 55.9M urban, so 67% rural; rural share used as an upper bound for the agricultural employment share: 1 - 0.67 = 0.33 (mid). Low reflects the loss of Ukraine's farmland in 1941-43; severe food shortage, Lend-Lease food.

annualCohort.note: Educated guess. Men reaching 18 per year (1926 class).

armor.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-6: Soviet tanks and SPGs 29,000 in 1944.

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess. Total combat aircraft read from Harrison 1998 Table 1-6; fighter share recalled, not read from a fetched source. Harrison 1998 Table 1-6: 33,200 combat aircraft in 1944 (Soviet Air Forces page: 40,241 aircraft of all types); ~17,000 fighters (split).

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess. Total combat aircraft read from Harrison 1998 Table 1-6; fighter share recalled, not read from a fetched source. Harrison 1998 Table 1-6: 33,200 combat aircraft less ~17,000 fighters (Il-2 ~11,000 in 1944).

artillery.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-6: 122,000 guns in 1944 (all calibres, as in the ussr-1941 snapshot).

ships_minor.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-6: 23 major naval vessels in 1944 (destroyers, submarines and larger); split guessed.

submarines.note: Part of the 23 major naval vessels of 1944.

air_defense.note: Educated guess. AA batteries' worth of guns per year.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Hard-surfaced roads; most of the occupied network destroyed.

majorPorts.note: Murmansk, Arkhangelsk, Vladivostok, Leningrad, Kronstadt, Batumi, Poti; Sevastopol and Odessa liberated April-May 1944.

merchantTonnage.note: League of Nations Year-Book 1939/40 table: Soviet merchant fleet 1,281,000 GRT (June 1938); war losses offset by ~40 Lend-Lease Liberty ships in the Pacific (high, educated guess). Converted to deadweight at x1.5 (low x1.3 of the low GRT, high x1.6 of the high GRT).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Bagration advanced ~500 km in five weeks on Lend-Lease trucks and rebuilt railways.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horse stock fell from ~21M in 1941 to ~8-10M; the Red Army still used ~1M horses.

chokepoints: Murmansk and Persian Corridor supply routes

homeDefense.note: 1.3 row: strategic depth, winter, partisan support behind German lines.

notes: Snapshot date June 1944 (Operation Bagration, 22 June). Territory = the USSR in its 1941 borders as claimed; Belorussia, the Baltic states and western Ukraine were still being liberated. The border uses world_1938 (nearest at or before 1944) and excludes the 1939-40 annexations, so areaKm2 mid is the claimed area. Forces are the whole Red Army, VVS, PVO and Navy incl. the Far East. Ship convention per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: battleships, carriers, cruisers and destroyers = ships_major, torpedo boats and smaller craft = ships_minor (role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries).
